tools.name: coordinate_bots
tools.description: Ask reachable Sagax teammates for advice (consult true) or assign concrete work. Give 1-4 bot_ids from list_bots and one message with exact file paths, constraints and what must be verified. Each call is its own assignment root: the answer carries a receipt (requestId) per teammate and a rootId. This external runtime is never resumed: read each result with assignment_status (a receipt's requestId, or rootId for the whole call), long-polling with wait_ms.

items.description: A teammate's name as your roster prints it, or its id ([id: …]) when the roster or list_bots shows one. A name shared by two reachable teammates is refused: use the id.

message.description: Question or task for these teammates; later requests in the same conversation can build on earlier ones. Send separate requests when responsibilities differ.

consult.description: True for a question the teammate answers from what it knows, acting on nothing. Default: work.

done_when.description: Harness-checked criterion: tool:ask_choice and/or first_line:PASS|FAIL (join with "; "). Free text is advisory. Unmet or a work-mode ack-only reply ends failed(incomplete).

tools.name: assignment_status
tools.description: Read-only: one assignment's status, outcome and result (give a coordinate_bots receipt's requestId, or the call's rootId), or, with no id, everything this runtime still waits on. Long-poll with wait_ms instead of being resumed. It starts nothing and changes nothing.

id.description: A coordinate_bots receipt's requestId, or its rootId. Omit to list every outstanding assignment.

wait_ms.description: Hold the answer up to this many milliseconds (at most 240000) for the assignment to settle.

tools.name: list_bots
tools.description: List the other bots (agents) you may contact in your own team and any additional teams the owner has explicitly allowed you to coordinate, with their team, model and current status. Call this to discover exact teammate IDs before assigning work or requesting advice through your available coordination tools.

tools.name: ask_bot
tools.description: Brief synchronous consultation with a reachable teammate. Quick replies return inline; busy or slow replies become asynchronous delegations with a task id. Use check_delegation or wait_delegation to retrieve their outcome. Use delegate_bot for assigning work. Existing peer approvals still apply.

bot_id.description: The target bot's id (from list_bots or your roster); a unique teammate name also resolves.

message.description: What to say / ask the bot.

tools.name: delegate_bot
tools.description: Hand work to a reachable teammate asynchronously. Returns a task id; the server dispatches when its source conversation and the peer are available and required approvals are granted. Use check_delegation or wait_delegation with that id; the external runtime does not need to end for polling.

bot_id.description: The target bot's id (from list_bots or your roster); a unique teammate name also resolves.

message.description: What the peer should do / answer.

reason.description: Optional one-line reason for the delegation (shown to the user as a chip).

tools.name: check_delegation
tools.description: Check one of this external runtime's delegations without waiting: queued, running, or finished with its result. Newly returned task ids can be checked immediately; the server enforces ownership and current peer access.

tools.name: wait_delegation
tools.description: Wait for one of this external runtime's delegations, including a newly returned task id, for up to timeout_seconds (maximum 240). Returns its result or current queued/running status; the server enforces ownership and current peer access.

timeout_seconds.description: give up waiting after this many seconds; default 60, max 240

tools.name: make_image
tools.description: Generate an image, or edit the image the person attached to their message ("put this person in Paris", "make it a watercolor", "remove the background"). With an image attached, it edits that image by default; set use_attached_image false to start from scratch. Uses the person's connected image provider (xAI Grok Imagine or OpenAI gpt-image), chosen automatically; this may incur API charges. The result is posted in this chat as your image: do not attach it again or describe it at length. Call it directly: no skill or tool search is needed.

prompt.description: What the image should show, or the change to make to the attached image, in the person's words.

image.description: Optional exact attachment path or /api/attachments URL of one image in the current person's message. Default: the latest image they attached.

use_attached_image.description: Default true: edit the image attached to the person's message when there is one.

tools.name: make_video
tools.description: Generate a video using the person's xAI API key, or the organization's granted xAI images and videos account. This may incur API charges. Native image_to_video and reference_to_video remain available when the engine offers them. generate starts an async job and returns job_id; status reads progress, list finds this conversation's jobs, cancel stops local polling/download, retry resumes the SAME upstream request without another paid generation. The completed MP4 is saved and attached in this chat. Never claim completion from pending status or show a temporary provider URL. Use a stable request_key for safe retries across turns. A new generate request_key starts a separately billable job.

prompt.description: What the video should show; required for generate.

image.description: Optional exact attachment path or /api/attachments URL for an image in the current person's message. No external URL or arbitrary file.

job_id.description: Returned job id; required for status, cancel and retry.

request_key.description: Stable identity for one generation. Same key and arguments reuse its job even across turns. Default: one generation per person request, including engine failover.

offset.description: For list: next_offset from the previous page; 20 jobs per page.
